title: SRE surveyor notes: graceful degradation, retry patterns, and quick mitigations for API bursts
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic reference for first responders when the API surface shows timeouts, 429s, degraded streams or rising error rates. This is intentionally lean — copy/paste friendly commands, signal->action mapping, and short notes to hand off to engineers.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated routing. Private deployments may have different network controls — call infra if VPC peering / NAT gates suspect.
- We assume metrics are coming from Prometheus (edge/api), traces in Jaeger/Tempo, logs in Loki, request sampling in Fastly/ingress. Replace with local equivalents if needed.
- Focused on production-first mitigations that avoid full rollback when possible.

Topline signals to watch (fast checks):
- 99th percentile latency for /v1/generate > baseline + 300ms over last 3m
- 5xx rate of >1% of requests (or >50 RPS errors) sustained for 5m
- 429 rate spike: >0.5% overall or >50 RPS throttled responses on a route
- Streaming disconnects: client-side disconnects + partial payload logs (pattern: stream.chunk_count < expected)
- Upstream model instance errors: kernel OOM, GPU driver faults surfaced in runtime error logs

Quick triage checklist (first responder):
1) Identify scope: which routes, which region, which model?
   - PromQL quick: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~"/v1/.*"}[1m])) by (route)
   - Error rate: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[1m])) by (route)
   - Throttle (429) query: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{status="429"}[1m])) by (route)
2) Check capacity/queue/backpressure:
   - Check cluster GPU utilization (grafana panel) and queue length metric: runtime_queue_length{pool="hosted-xx"}
3) Check rollout/faults: any recent model rollout or infra deploy in last 30m?
   - Query deployment events: kubectl get events --namespace=redwood --field-selector type=Warning --since=30m
4) Gather logs/traces: sample 5 trace ids for affected requests and attach to incident.

Fast mitigations (safe order):
A. Apply short-term rate-limiting adjustment (soft): increase client rate quota for low-tier routes? NO — usually reduce not increase. Instead: temporarily *raise* throttling for noisy keys to protect SLOs. Use console to bump rate limit or apply block list for bad tokens.
B. Turn off expensive features: streaming + heavy re-ranking + tool-calls. For streaming degradation, flip to non-streaming mode (buffered) via routing policy or feature flag.
C. Route to cheaper/faster model variant (fallback): use routing policy to send new requests to model-variant:vX-compact. This preserves availability at lower quality.
D. Enable burst/overflow pool if Dedicated has reserved burst capacity.
E. Autoscaler: if backlog is growth and GPU utilization < 95%, increase replica target (scale-out) or trigger manual capacity (for Dedicated).
F. If cause is kernel/OOM or driver faults, cordon affected node(s) and rollout model instances onto healthy nodes.

Failure-mode specific play snippets:

1) TIMEOUTS (high latency or request timeouts)
- Indicators: tail latency up, many requests hit proxy response timeout, traces show long queue times not just model generation time.
- Likely causes: queuing at frontend, overloaded GPU, slow model variant, KV cache miss storm, cold KV caches.
- Immediate actions:
  - Check queue depth: curl -s "${GRAFANA_API}/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=runtime_queue_length"
  - If queue depth > threshold -> apply temporary rate-limit per-client group, or reduce batch sizes: patch autoscaler: kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'
  - Toggle caching tier to aggressive (turn on prefix-KV cache for hot routes) via console patch
  - Fallback: route to smaller model (vX-compact) using routing policy ID in console
- Notes: don't restart all pods at once; that amplifies cold starts. Restart strategy: rolling restart with 1 pod at a time.

2) 429s (rate limiting / client bursts)
- Indicators: upstream service returning 429 with body code throttle, spikes correlate with client keys or route.
- Likely causes: sudden client retry storms, policy mis-config, autoscaler lag.
- Immediate actions:
  - Identify top offending API keys: query logs for status=429 | top_by(api_key, count)
  - Apply soft blocks: add offending keys to temporary throttled list in console or apply token-scoped rate-limit decrease.
  - Communicate to product/GTM: send immediate message to account contact if spikes are due to a single customer.
  - If system-wide 429s -> increase capacity (burst pool) or route non-critical traffic to degraded model.

3) DEGRADED STREAMING (partial frames, client disconnects)
- Indicators: increased stream.reset, stream.chunk_errors, client reconnects, logs with 'incomplete-chunk'
- Likely causes: network flakiness between edge and runtime, client aborts, memory pressure leading to partial flushes, streaming buffer threshold reached.
- Immediate actions:
  - Toggle clients to buffered responses: console flag to force buffered mode for the affected route. Reduces client-perceived real-time but improves success rate.
  - Reduce chunk size / lower streaming window in runtime configuration.
  - Monitor network egress error rates for node pools; if spike -> cordon nodes and shift traffic.
  - If streaming failing only for certain regions, reroute that region to fallback region.

4) ELEVATED ERROR RATES (5xx spike)
- Indicators: 502/500/503 increasing; stack traces show model runtime exceptions or dependency timeouts.
- Likely causes: model binary crash, infra networking, dependent auth service down.
- Immediate actions:
  - Grab representative logs: logs | grep "exception" | head -n 100 and attach to ticket
  - If model process crash -> quick rollback to previous model version + patch scheduling: use console to pin model to previous stable version
  - If dependency (auth, kv store) showing errors -> fail open vs. fail closed decision: prefer fail open for read-only paths; get infra on call for dependency outage.

Operator-level commands (copy/paste):
- List pods with high restarts: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, restarts: .status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}' | sort -r -k2
- Rolling restart single deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-deployment -n redwood --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-deployment && sleep 30 && check health
- Tail recent logs for route X: kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n redwood --since=10m | grep "route=/v1/generate" | tail -n 500

Sample PromQLs (quick paste):
- 95p latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="edge"}[5m])) by (le, route))
- 429 rate: sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{status="429"}[1m])) by (route)
- queue length: max(runtime_queue_length{pool=~".*"}) by (pool)

Communications templates:
- Slack incident starter (channel #sre-incidents):
  "INCIDENT: v1/generate high 99p latency in us-west-2. Impact: some requests timing out. Triage in progress. Actions: throttling noisy keys, routing to compact model. Pager: Asha. ETA for recovery: 15m. Logs attached: <link>"
- Customer-facing note (short):
  "We are investigating elevated timeouts impacting text generation in us-west-2. Some requests may be slower; we have applied mitigation and will update in 30 minutes. If you observe production impact, please reply to this thread with request IDs."

Post-incident follow-ups (TODO list):
- Add a metric for client burst concentration (top-10 tokens share) to detect noisy customers earlier
- Improve streaming sentinel that auto-forces buffered mode for 3m after X stream resets
- Run a chaos test simulating KV cache cold storm to quantify cold-start cost and recovery time
- Create a dashboard showing model-variant fallbacks over time

Escalation notes:
- If you see GPU kernel OOMs or driver panics, escalate to infra+runtime immediately (pager: on-call infra, tag: gpu)
- If >30% of requests are hitting degraded variant for >30m, consider a rollback to previous stable config and open an RCA.

Notes to self / rough ideas (raw):
- Could we add a short-circuit 'safety valve' that automatically reduces batch sizes when queue latency > X? Need to model token cost effect.
- Consider a client advisory API that returns 'safeRate' header for SDKs to back off adaptively.
- Investigate whether some 429s are client-level retry loops — add jitter guidance in SDK.

Open questions (for product/eng):
- What SLAs do we want to promise for streamed vs buffered responses? (SLA parity probably impossible)
- Can Dedicated customers opt-in to a different default fallback (e.g., degrade to offline cached completions instead of smaller model)?

Hand-off checklist when passing incident to eng: attach:
- Top 10 traces (link)
- Top offending API keys + sample request IDs
- Exact console toggles performed (rate limits, routing policy IDs)
- Time series snapshot (png) for 99/95/50 latencies, error rates, and queue depths
- Suggested next steps and possible regressions to watch for

Appendix: quick references / links
- Runtime health dashboard: <grafana>/d/runtime-overview
- Fallback routing docs: confluence://product/routing-fallbacks
- SDK retry guidance: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/blob/main/RETRY.md

End of file — keep this one lightweight and iteratively expand as we hit more corner cases.
